title: Against the Valentinians
author: tertullian
attributionNote: The attribution is recorded as the edition and the scholarly consensus give it; where the attribution is disputed, the work says so.
description: A satirical account and refutation of the Valentinian Gnostic system, its aeons, its myth of Sophia and its division of humanity. Hostile in tone and not a neutral report, but a principal source for the system as Latin Christians encountered it.
historicalContext: Written in Carthage after Tertullian joined the Montanists, against a Gnostic school that had spread in Rome and North Africa.
availabilityNote: Streamed from the Christian Classics Ethereal Library at read time. Holmes's translation from the Ante-Nicene Fathers, served by the CCEL. The text reports the system it opposes; its characterisations are Tertullian's.
